# Jubilees Chapter 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Isaac Weaned; Hagar Cast Out; Mastema Challenges Abraham

---

**17:1** In the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee, Isaac was weaned. Abraham threw a great feast in the third month to celebrate.

**17:2** Ishmael, son of the Egyptian Hagar, was there with his father Abraham. Abraham was overjoyed, blessing God that he had lived to see both his sons and had not died without children.

**17:3** He thought back to the words God had spoken to him the day Lot walked away from him, and he rejoiced that God had given him descendants on the earth — people who would inherit the land. He praised the Creator of all things with his whole heart.

**17:4** But Sarah watched Ishmael laughing and dancing, and Abraham beaming with joy, and jealousy rose up in her. She told Abraham: "Get rid of this slave woman and her son. That slave's son is not going to share the inheritance with my son Isaac."

**17:5** This hit Abraham hard — he was deeply troubled for his son's sake.

**17:6** God said to Abraham: "Don't be troubled over the boy or over his mother. Listen to Sarah in everything she tells you — because it is through Isaac that your name and legacy will continue."

**17:7** "But I will also make a nation of the slave woman's son, because he is your blood."

**17:8** Abraham got up early the next morning, packed bread and a skin of water, slung it over Hagar's shoulder, and sent her and the child away.

**17:9** She wandered into the wilderness around Beersheba. When the water ran out, the child grew desperately thirsty. He couldn't walk anymore and collapsed under a tree.

**17:10** His mother picked him up and laid him under the tree, then walked away — about an arrow's flight off — and sat down. She said: "I can't watch my child die."

**17:11** She sat there sobbing. Then the angel of God called down to Hagar from heaven: "What's the matter, Hagar? Don't be afraid — God has heard the boy crying, right where he is."

**17:12** "Get up. Go to him. Hold him in your arms. I will make him a great nation."

**17:13** God opened her eyes and she saw a spring of water. She ran to it, filled the skin, and brought the boy water. He drank and came back to life.

**17:14** Ishmael grew up in the wilderness and became a skilled archer.

**17:15** God stayed with him, and his mother found him a wife from Egypt.

**17:16** In the seventh week, first year, first month of this jubilee — on the twelfth day of the month — voices broke out in heaven about Abraham. They said he was completely faithful in everything God had told him, that he truly loved the LORD, and that through every hardship he had never wavered.

**17:17** At that moment, the prince Mastema stepped forward before God: "Look at Abraham — he loves Isaac more than anything in the world. Tell him to offer Isaac as a burnt offering on the altar. Then you'll see whether he'll actually do it, and you'll know if his faithfulness is real."

**17:18** The LORD knew already that Abraham was faithful through everything — he had been tested by the call to leave his homeland, by famine, by the wealth and threats of kings, by the taking of his wife, by circumcision, and by sending away Ishmael and Hagar.

**17:19** In every test he came through with his integrity intact. He never grew impatient. He never dragged his feet. He was faithful, and his love for the LORD was genuine.

---
*PNEUMA notes: Mastema's challenge (vv.16-17) is rendered as a dramatic courtroom scene — the adversary presenting a formal challenge to God. The seven prior tests (v.18) are listed as evidence of Abraham's track record. The parallel with Job 1 is clear and deliberate in Jubilees.*
